items.title: Local normal collar charts at a smooth spacelike hypersurface

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity, Cambridge lecture notes, October 12 2022 revision, §§3.3–3.4, printed pp. 37–39 (PDF pp. 38–40)
David Tong, General Relativity, Cambridge Part III lecture notes, Chapter 3, §§3.3.1–3.3.2, printed pp. 120–122 (chapter PDF pp. 30–32)

items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold, and let $i:\Sigma\to M$ be a smooth
spacelike embedding. Suppose a smooth future unit normal field $n$ along
$i(\Sigma)$ is supplied. For every $p\in\Sigma$ there are an open
neighborhood $U_p\subseteq\Sigma$, a number $\epsilon_p>0$, and an open
$V_p\subseteq M$ such that the restricted map
$\Phi_p:(-\epsilon_p,\epsilon_p)\times U_p\to V_p$ given by

$$\Phi_p(t,x)=\gamma_{i(x),n_{i(x)}}(t)$$

is a diffeomorphism, where $\gamma_{q,v}$ is the maximal affinely
parameterized metric geodesic with initial data $(q,v)$. At its center,

$$d(\Phi_p)_{(0,p)}(a\partial_t+X)=a n_{i(p)}+d i_p(X).$$

The neighborhoods and time widths may depend on $p$; no globally injective
normal exponential map or uniform width is asserted.

items.title: Closed two-forms agreeing on a Cauchy slice differ by an exact form

references.title: Victor Guillemin and Peter Haine, Differential Forms, MIT 18.952 text (2019), §2.6, Theorem 2.6.15 and Exercise 2.6.iv, printed pp. 64–66

items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and Dependent Choice. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth
time-oriented globally hyperbolic Lorentzian four-manifold, and let
$i:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$ be a smooth spacelike Cauchy embedding. If
$F,\bar F\in\Omega^2(M)$ are smooth closed two-forms with
$i^*F=i^*\bar F$, then $F-\bar F$ is exact: there is a smooth
$\alpha\in\Omega^1(M)$ such that $d\alpha=F-\bar F$.

Here a closed form has zero exterior derivative, and exactness means being the
exterior derivative of a globally defined smooth form, as in
[[def-de-rham-cohomology]].

items.title: Local evolution of the adopted electrovacuum model
items.physical_scope: Conditional local evolution in the selected smooth, source-free, zero-matter-action Einstein-Maxwell branch. It covers the stated periodic high-Sobolev class and arbitrary smooth constrained data locally, subject to magnetic compatibility with one supplied normalized circle-bundle sector; electric initial data remain independent smooth data. There is no uniform noncompact time width, global-time, maximal-development, or empirical-validity claim.

references.title: P. T. Chruściel, An introduction to the Cauchy problem for the Einstein equations, Roscoff lecture notes (2011), complete 132-page notes, §1.6, printed pp. 23–25 (PDF pp. 27–29)
references.locator: The covariant source-free Maxwell two-form, electric/magnetic split, Einstein coupling, Lorenz-gauge Cauchy system and Maxwell constraint propagation. The source uses a global potential and supplies no coupled local existence proof.

references.title: M. Alcubierre, J. C. Degollado and M. Salgado, The Einstein-Maxwell system in 3+1 form and initial data for multiple charged black holes, arXiv:0907.1151v2 (2009), complete 20-page paper
references.locator: §§II.1–II.3, PDF pp. 3–8, Maxwell field-strength evolution, divergence constraints, electromagnetic stress and Einstein constraints. Gaussian normalization and the paper's opposite K sign are not imported; its Einstein evolution discussion explicitly does not prove coupled local existence.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity, Cambridge lecture notes, 12 October 2022 revision, complete 125-page notes
references.locator: §6.2, equation (6.8), covariant Maxwell equations; §6.3, equations (6.27)–(6.28), electromagnetic stress and its source-free conservation exercise; §10.4, constraints. Gaussian normalization and c=1 conventions are not imported.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty
smooth oriented three-manifold without boundary, with smooth Riemannian metric
$h$, smooth symmetric covariant tensor $K$, and smooth tangent vector fields
$e,b$. Fix $\kappa>0$, $\mu_0>0$, and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and use the
signature, SI conventions, and electromagnetic stress tensor of
[[def-emg-geometry-units]] and [[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]].
Assume $(\Sigma,h,K,e,b)$ satisfies all four source-free constraints of
[[def-emg-constrained-electrovacuum-data]].

In the periodic case $\Sigma=\mathbb T^3_{2\pi}$, for an integer $s\ge5$,
also consider smooth data with $h\in H^{s+1}$, $K,e,b\in H^s$, and the
uniform lower eigenvalue bound $h\ge c_0I$ for some $c_0>0$ specified by
[[def-emg-periodic-high-sobolev-state]]. On its common local interval the
field-strength solution has
$g\in L^\infty H^{s+1}\cap C^0H^s$,
$\partial_tg\in L^\infty H^s\cap C^0H^{s-1}$, and
$F\in L^\infty H^s\cap C^0H^{s-1}$, with the time coordinate measured in
length units as in [[def-emg-geometry-units]].

For the magnetic data define the smooth two-form
$\beta_b(X,Y):=\operatorname{vol}_h(b,X,Y)$. Assume the following explicit
initial bundle compatibility: there are a countable open cover $(U_i)$ of
$\Sigma$, smooth transition maps $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to U(1)$, smooth local
real one-forms $a_i$, and one constant $\kappa_0>0$. Require
$g_{ii}=1$, $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$ on triple overlaps, and
$a_j=a_i+\lambda(g_{ij})$ on every overlap, where
$\lambda(g)=-i g^{-1}dg$; also require $\kappa_0\,da_i=\beta_b$ on $U_i$.
Here $\kappa_0$
has units weber and the normalized local forms have the units in
[[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]. This is the fixed
normalized circle-bundle sector of [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]];
it imposes no global real-valued potential and no condition on the independent
electric data beyond the stated constraints.

In the action model of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-action]], choose the
zero-matter branch: the matter configuration space is a singleton and
$S_m\equiv0$, so its current and Hilbert tensor vanish. Then there is a smooth
time-oriented local development of the source-free system on a neighborhood
of the entire initial surface, after restriction to a possibly variable-width
globally hyperbolic Cauchy neighborhood. Its electromagnetic two-form is the
curvature of a smooth connection in the supplied normalized circle-bundle
sector, and its initial electric and magnetic fields are exactly $e,b$.
Any two such developments are related near the initial surface by a
data-fixing, time-orientation-preserving isometry carrying the metric and
two-form to one another. This is a conditional model deduction; it asserts
neither physical validity, a uniform positive time width for noncompact
$\Sigma$, global-time existence, nor a maximal-development result.

items.title: Electromagnetic conservation in source-free curved spacetime
items.physical_scope: A local model deduction for the smooth zero-matter-action Einstein-Maxwell branch on a Lorentzian four-manifold. It asserts covariant conservation of electromagnetic stress on stationary source-free configurations only; it does not assert existence, global energy conservation, or empirical validity.

references.title: H. S. Reall, Part III General Relativity, Cambridge lecture notes, 12 October 2022 revision, complete 125-page notes
references.locator: §6.2, equation (6.8), curved-spacetime Maxwell equations; §6.3, equations (6.27)–(6.28), the Maxwell stress tensor and its source-free conservation exercise. Gaussian normalization is not imported.

references.title: M. Alcubierre, J. C. Degollado and M. Salgado, The Einstein-Maxwell system in 3+1 form and initial data for multiple charged black holes, arXiv:0907.1151v2 (2009), complete 20-page paper
references.locator: §II.2, equations (2.70)–(2.78), electromagnetic stress tensor, trace and observer projections. The Gaussian 1/(4π) factor is replaced by the stated SI μ0 normalization.

items.statement:
Adopt the zero-matter specialization of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-action]]:
the matter functional is identically zero on a singleton matter configuration
space, so its current and Hilbert tensor vanish. Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be a smooth,
time-oriented, oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$,
and let $F$ be the smooth physical curvature two-form of a connection in a
fixed normalized circle-bundle sector, with the local $F=\kappa_0 da_i$
convention of [[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]]. If the adopted compact-variation action is
stationary, then its electromagnetic stress tensor

$$T^{\rm EM}_{ab}=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right)$$

obeys

$$\nabla^aT^{\rm EM}_{ab}=0.$$
This is a local conditional deduction for the stated classical model. It does
not assert a global conserved energy, existence of a stationary configuration,
or empirical validity.

items.title: Maximal smooth Cauchy development of adopted electrovacuum
items.physical_scope: Conditional universal smooth globally hyperbolic development for the zero-matter-action Einstein-Maxwell field-strength model, with initial data in one supplied normalized circle-bundle sector. Maximality is within smooth globally hyperbolic developments; no geodesic completeness, rough or non-globally-hyperbolic extension maximality, global-time estimate, or empirical-validity claim is made.

references.title: J. Sbierski, On the Existence of a Maximal Cauchy Development for the Einstein Equations — a Dezornification, arXiv:1309.7591v3 (2015), Definitions and Theorems 2.6–2.8, printed pp. 10–12, and complete proofs §§3.1–3.3, printed pp. 12–24
references.locator: The source is vacuum-only. Its smooth set-sized gluing and maximality argument is used only through the current mathematical EMG supplier, whose local existence and uniqueness obligations are separately supplied.

references.title: P. T. Chruściel, An introduction to the Cauchy problem for the Einstein equations, Roscoff lecture notes (2011), complete 132-page notes, especially §1.6, printed pp. 23–25 (PDF pp. 27–29)
references.locator: Source-free Einstein-Maxwell Cauchy formulation and the distinction between Maxwell constraints and evolution. The notes use a global potential; no such global potential is assumed here.

items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a nonempty
connected smooth oriented three-manifold without boundary, with smooth
Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$, and smooth tangent vector
fields $e,b$. Fix $\kappa>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, and the SI
Lorentzian conventions of [[def-emg-geometry-units]]. Assume the four
constraints of [[def-emg-constrained-electrovacuum-data]]. Define
$\beta_b(X,Y)=\operatorname{vol}_h(b,X,Y)$, and supply a countable cover
$(U_i)$, transition maps $g_{ij}:U_i\cap U_j\to U(1)$, local real one-forms
$a_i$, and $\kappa_0>0$ satisfying $g_{ii}=1$, $g_{ij}g_{jk}=g_{ik}$,
$a_j=a_i+\lambda(g_{ij})$, and $\kappa_0 da_i=\beta_b$, where
$\lambda(g)=-i g^{-1}dg$. These are the normalized local data of
[[def-emg-local-potentials-and-circle-data]] restricted to the initial slice.
Adopt the zero-matter action branch
$S_m\equiv0$ of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-action]].

Then there is a smooth connected time-oriented globally hyperbolic
development $(M_{\max},g_{\max},F_{\max},i_{\max})$ of the source-free
[[def-emg-electrovacuum-cauchy-system]] with the complete data $(h,K,e,b)$.
The two-form $F_{\max}=\kappa_0 f_{\max}$ is the physical curvature of a
smooth connection in the bundle sector obtained by transporting the supplied
initial sector over a Cauchy product. Here $f_{\max}\in\Omega^2(M_{\max})$
is its normalized curvature, locally $f_{\max}=da_i$; the supplied constant
$\kappa_0>0$ has units Wb, so multiplication gives the SI physical curvature.
Every other smooth globally hyperbolic development with the same complete data
for which the adopted action is stationary embeds into this one by a
time-orientation-preserving isometric embedding that fixes $\Sigma$ and carries
$F$ to $F_{\max}$. Any two maximal developments are related by exactly one
data-fixing isometry of $(g,F)$. Maximality is within the smooth globally
hyperbolic solution class; it asserts no geodesic completeness, no maximality
among rough or non-globally-hyperbolic extensions, no global-in-time
regularity estimate, and no empirical validity.

items.title: Adopted parallel-field initial state
items.physical_scope: An exact smooth-data example in the zero-matter-action Einstein-Maxwell model on a flat three-torus. It supplies compatible expanding initial data with nonzero parallel electric and magnetic fields and invokes only the conditional local-development theorem; it asserts no isotropy at later times or empirical observation.

references.title: M. Alcubierre, J. C. Degollado and M. Salgado, The Einstein-Maxwell system in 3+1 form and initial data for multiple charged black holes, arXiv:0907.1151v2 (2009), complete 20-page paper
references.locator: §II.3, equations (2.79)–(2.80), electromagnetic Hamiltonian and momentum constraints; §II.2, equations (2.70)–(2.78), electromagnetic energy and momentum projections. The local calculation uses the exact declared SI and K conventions.

references.title: P. T. Chruściel, An introduction to the Cauchy problem for the Einstein equations, Roscoff lecture notes (2011), complete 132-page notes
references.locator: §1.6, printed pp. 23–25 (PDF pp. 27–29), source-free Einstein-Maxwell Cauchy formulation and electric/magnetic initial fields. No existence conclusion is imported from this section.

items.statement:
Let $L>0$ be the physical side length of
$\mathbb T^3_L=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$, with length coordinates
$(X,Y,Z)$ and flat metric $h=dX^2+dY^2+dZ^2$. Give $\mathbb T^3_L$ the
orientation $dX\wedge dY\wedge dZ$. Fix the normalized circle-flux scale
$\kappa_0>0$ from [[def-emg-geometry-units]], and set
$$B_0:=\frac{2\pi\kappa_0}{L^2},\qquad H:=\sqrt{\frac{\kappa}{3\mu_0}}\,B_0.$$
Take $\Lambda=0$ and define $K=Hh$, $e=B_0\partial_Z$, and
$b=B_0\partial_Z$. The electric and magnetic observer fields are nonzero
and parallel in this initial state.

The magnetic two-form is
$\beta_b=B_0\,dX\wedge dY$. It is compatible with a nontrivial normalized
circle bundle, not just a globally defined potential: on the universal cover
$\mathbb R^3\times U(1)$, with $z\in U(1)$, use the connection one-form
$$\omega=-i z^{-1}dz+\frac{2\pi}{L^2}X\,dY.$$
Let the deck transformations be
$$T_X(X,Y,Z,z)=(X+L,Y,Z,e^{-2\pi iY/L}z),\quad T_Y(X,Y,Z,z)=(X,Y+L,Z,z),\quad T_Z(X,Y,Z,z)=(X,Y,Z+L,z).$$
They commute because $e^{-2\pi i(Y+L)/L}=e^{-2\pi iY/L}$. The one-form
$\omega$ is invariant under these identifications, so it descends to a
connection on the quotient bundle over $\mathbb T^3_L$. Its curvature is
$$d\omega=\frac{2\pi}{L^2}dX\wedge dY,$$
hence the physical curvature $\kappa_0d\omega$ is exactly $\beta_b$.

The diagram shows one fundamental square in the $X,Y$ directions. The
opposite vertical edges are glued with the displayed $U(1)$ transition; the
horizontal edges are glued without a fiber twist. It records the quotient
convention but is not used in the verification.

  \draw[->,thick] (-0.35,0.2) -- (-0.35,2.8)
    node[midway,left] {$Y$};
  \draw[->,thick] (0.2,-0.35) -- (3.8,-0.35)
    node[midway,below] {$X$};
  \draw[->,blue,thick] (0,0.35) -- (0,2.65);
